firstPrompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: ONE full-body illustrated IRONWALL SENTINEL enemy sprite for Parry Tower, transparent RGBA. This is a pose rework of image 1, not a redesign.
INPUT ROLES: Image 1 is the character DESIGN and exact PAINTED STYLE reference. Images 2 and 3 are two views of a real 3D sword-and-shield study, for spatial reasoning ONLY: shield protects torso, bent shield elbow, body weight supported by legs, room to swing sword. Do not reproduce its gray mannequin, UI, floor, sword design, camera elevation, extreme squat or its weapon handedness.
KEEP CHARACTER: same stout chunky knight, broad flat-topped enclosed helmet and narrow amber visor, chipped silver / blue-gray plate armor, worn brass edging, huge rectangular tower shield with brass cross and round boss, dark teal scarf and short torn teal tabard, heavy angular boots. Same thick irregular black ink outlines, angular carefully painted weathered metal, deep black shadows, illustrated game-art finish and compact stylized proportions of image 1.
REBUILD THE ENTIRE POSE: enemy stands at screen RIGHT and looks toward screen LEFT. Use a low eye-level three-quarter view from the character's anatomical LEFT (sword-arm) side, enough side view to read the direction. Helmet, ribs, hips and knees all consistently face toward the left-side opponent; do not twist the chest to face the viewer.
Weapons are explicitly LEFT-HANDED: anatomical LEFT hand holds the sword; anatomical RIGHT arm holds the tower shield. These are the character's own sides, not the viewer's. Left sword arm is on the camera-near side. Right shield arm is on the far side. Establish the whole torso and both shoulders consistently with that handedness.
NEW GUARD: the large shield is raised upright ahead of the body toward screen-left, tilted slightly inward to protect neck, chest and abdomen from the left-side opponent. Shield lower tip just above ground; top approximately shoulder height. Right elbow bent naturally behind shield, shield supported by believable forearm and rear grip; right shoulder -> upper arm -> elbow -> forearm -> shield is continuous, even where hidden. Do not reach the shield arm fully straight. Body tucked behind shield relative to opponent.
The LEFT sword arm is drawn BACK AND LOW beside the near-side waist at screen-right, shoulder relaxed, elbow bent about 90 degrees, elbow behind wrist, preparing a rising or diagonal cut. Gauntlet at belt/hip level, unmistakably a LEFT hand, wraps firmly around the sword hilt with four articulated curled fingers and a separately opposed thumb near the guard. Thumb emerges from the correct thumb side of the LEFT palm and crosses the grip; palm, wrist and forearm form one coherent volume. No second right hand. Do not merely mirror a hand pasted onto an old arm.
Sword points backward toward screen-right and slightly downward, blade fully outside the body silhouette and clear of boots, shield and cloth; straight sturdy blade and hilt on one axis. This is a restrained ready guard, not a stabbing or extended attack pose. Leave a readable gap around the sword hand and forearm so its grip can be inspected. No blade over the head or across the chest.
Feet planted firmly at common ground baseline: shield-side lead foot toward screen-left, sword-side rear foot screen-right, knees softly bent, moderate wide stable stance, not an extreme crouch, lunge, walk or run. Cloth stays behind arms and above feet. Use the full-body silhouette with all helmet, feet, shield, sword tip visible and generous transparent margins. Broad near sword-hand at useful readable scale; not hidden by shield.
OUTPUT: one assembled, finished illustrated character only. Genuine transparent background. No gray or white backdrop, no grid, floor, shadow, scenery, writing, labels, inset, reference panel, duplicate figure or 3D render. Maintain the original beautiful painted style.
correctionPrompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit, full pose correction of this illustrated sentinel. Keep this exact beautiful thick black ink and textured painted-metal style, proportions, colors, helmet, teal cloth, brass cross tower shield and sword design. Keep true transparent background and full-body framing with sword tip and feet inside margins.
Change the body and shield composition substantially to a tightly guarded fighting stance inspired by the second input 3D study. Bring the TOWER SHIELD inward toward the center of the image so it overlaps and conceals most of the breastplate and the shield-side shoulder, instead of being held out to the far left. Raise shield top to lower-helmet height. Lean the head, chest and pelvis forward toward screen-left and tuck them behind the raised shield. Body is turned much more in profile toward the left-side enemy, with the rear shoulder drawn back to screen-right, no broad front-facing display of the chest. Lower the hips and bend both knees a little more for planted defensive readiness. Keep the two boots firmly planted, shield-side lead foot left, rear foot right. This must look like actively guarding behind a large shield, not posing with a shield beside the body. The shield must still show its brass cross and round boss.
Keep sword drawn back beside the waist on the camera-near LEFT arm, with forearm and hand clearly connected and visible to the right of the body; blade extends backward screen-right, a little down, clear of cloth and feet. Anatomical LEFT hand grips sword and anatomical RIGHT hand/arm supports shield, taking account of the entire torso and shoulders. Make a coherent left sword gauntlet: four curled fingers wrap the grip, thumb on its anatomically correct side and opposing the fingers, wrist not twisted backwards. No extra fingers or hands. Preserve the old character design but reconstruct pose naturally. No overhead sword, no 3D gray model, no floor, UI, labels or inset. One finished illustrated character.
